text: Businessman/Councilmember

When I first ran for city council, it was because many of you believed our community was ready for change. You wanted business growth, community events and a stronger future. Over the years, I have worked hard to honor that trust and turn those goals into real progress.

Today, I am standing before you again, not just because of what we have accomplished, but because you have asked me to continue this work. That not only means a lot to me, but what it could mean for our community.

Together, we have made meaningful strides. We have expanded opportunities for local businesses, bringing in more places to shop. Places such as Costco, Walmart, Hobby Lobby and Trader Joe's are a few businesses that have strengthened our local economy while creating local jobs. We have prioritized open spaces that give families and neighbors places to gather and connect, especially with the recent development of Vin Scully Centennial Park. We have taken important steps toward building a safer community where people feel secure, making us one of the safest cities in Orange County.

At the same time, we have invested in the rehabilitation of our streets, improving roads, building water pump stations, ensuring we have an adequate water supply and accessible sidewalks, ensuring safer travel for everyone in our community. I accomplished all this while maintaining a balanced budget each year.
I was honored to be recognized as City Elected Leader of the Year by the Association of California Cities.

These accomplishments did not happen overnight and they were not achieved alone. They are the result of listening to you, working alongside you and staying committed to what matters most for our city.

But there is still more to do. On the heels of our Centennial comes new opportunities and new challenges, but I know that we can overcome them. I am ready to keep building on the progress we have made, to keep pushing for smart development, to protect what makes our city special and to ensure that every resident benefits from the work we are doing.

I am proud of the progress that we have made together and am ready to keep moving our community forward. With your support, I will continue to work hard to deliver the results you deserve and build a future that reflects our potential as a city.
I’m proudly endorsed by our police, firefighters, teachers and parents.

text: Mayor City of La Habra

My name is Jose Medrano, I currently serve as Mayor of La Habra. My wife and I have been fortunate enough to raise our daughters in our community and local schools. As a public safety advocate and law enforcement officer, I feel it is important to be engaged in our community and help keep it safe. As a Mexican Immigrant and U.S. Citizen, I find it important to include public service in my life and help those who seek the same opportunity. I have over 30 years of Law Enforcement experience. I am a retired Detective for the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s office having investigated Human Trafficking, Juvenile crimes and other criminal investigations. I have a B.A. in Business Administration from CSUF. As a father I strongly believe in education. Two of my daughters are graduates of University of California schools and one attends USD as a student athlete.

I have been committed to making local government more efficient, responsive and accountable to everyone.I continue to make Public Safety a priority through my in person “Crime Watch” meetings in various neighborhoods throughout the City of La Habra. Through my leadership on the council I continue to support the city’s fiscally responsible direction resulting in balanced budgets. The city has completed significant capital improvement projects and road improvements. My support of open spaces and the revitalization of parks continues with the recent opening of the Dog Park and other amenities at Centennial Park and improvements at other parks. As Mayor I continue to support our efforts to address traffic through signal synchronization on Imperial Highway, Lambert Road, Hacienda Blvd, Whittier Blvd and traffic calming measures in various neighborhoods. I have addressed the homeless issue in La Habra by supporting our efforts with our two homeless shelters in neighboring cities and staffing two homeless outreach liaisons. I continue to support our La Habra Businesses through my weekly Business of the Week promotion on social media. I am endorsed by the La Habra Police Association, LA County Firefighters IAFF 1014, Teachers and Community advocates in La Habra.

text: Retired Teacher

La Habra is my home. My husband and I bought our house 43 years ago and we never left! Fondly known as Dr.P., I taught at Washington Middle School in the La Habra City School District for nearly 33 years, teaching more than 7000 students. I hold a Bachelors, Masters, and Doctorate degree as well as several teaching credentials.
Since retiring. I served as a Trustee on the La Habra City School District School Board and help La Habra non-profits. Serving both our residents and our local businesses gives me unique insights for prioritizing our La Habra’s needs.
Unfortunately, we have seen our City Council campaign on pledges of “no new taxes” only to have them push for higher sales taxes. Our City Council failed to get a housing element approved in a timely manner, opening the door to “builder’s remedy” housing development the city can’t stop.
Incredibly, the City Council sent our tax dollars to a Chamber of Commerce in Buena Park while refusing to support our La Habra Chamber of Commerce.
I will restore trust in our City Council by supporting term limits, keeping my promises, and putting La Habra first. I promise all my Council stipends will go to La Habra non-profits!
I would be honored to have your vote. www.electpritchard.com www.DrPstem.com

text: IT Analyst/Instructor

I am a husband, father, educator, and information technology professional who believes public service should begin with giving, not taking. My family and I proudly call La Habra home, and I am running for City Council to bring practical experience, fresh ideas, and accountable leadership to City Hall.

I support reasonable term limits because elected office should be temporary public service, not a lifelong career. New voices and fair opportunities to serve strengthen local government. I will advocate for a meaningful term-limits measure.

If elected, I will not personally keep City Council compensation. I am running because I love this community and believe public service should be rooted in sacrifice, integrity, and commitment rather than personal gain.

I hold bachelor's and master's degrees in information technology and management, teach college technology courses, and have experience in private industry, state government, healthcare, cybersecurity, and public service. I will focus on fiscal responsibility, public safety, reliable infrastructure, transparent government, strong local businesses, quality parks, support for families, and responsive city services.
I would be honored to earn your trust and respectfully ask for your vote.
